blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel.
Tour of the Brazilian side of the waterfalls with an English-speaking guide.
Located  on the border of Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay, the Iguazu Falls are 275 huge streams of water that fall from a terrible height. The waterfalls are located in a national park with unique flora and fauna, arose as a result of a volcanic eruption and the displacement of the earth's strata. The name of the waterfalls means "big water" in Guarani. 275 waterfalls, each of which has its own name, fall with a roar into the Devil's Throat Gorge.  The contrast between the calm and even lazy flow of the waters  of the Iguazu River  above the waterfalls and the powerful throwing of bubbling streams of water from a height of 72 meters into the abyss is amazing. You can stand for hours without looking up, contemplating this spectacle and thinking about the splendor and eternity of our universe. 
In addition,  you can book a visit to the Bird Park (USD 50 P/P). It is located near the Iguazu National Park. You will enter huge aviaries, in which amazing, fabulous birds of outlandish colors fly or walk freely among the rainforest.
In addition,  you can book a "Makuco Safari" trip (USD 130 P/P). You will drive through the jungle in an open jeep for about 3 kilometers, accompanied by a guide who will tell you a lot of interesting things about the ecology of the region. Then you will go on foot to the banks  of the Iguazu River, from where you will be taken by motor boat close to the waterfalls.
